newsitem.title: USA: Fisher Scientific sinks on rev forecast.
newsitem.headline: Fisher Scientific sinks on rev forecast.

text.p: Shares of Fisher Scientific International Inc dropped almost 14 percent after the company said it expects its near-term revenue growth to remain below historical levels due to soft demand in the clinical laboratory market.
Shares of the scientific equipment supplier dropped 5-3/4 to 36-3/8 in heavy trading, with more than 17 times the normal volume of shares changing hands.

Hampton, N.H.-based Fisher also said it continues to evaluate areas to improve efficiency. The company expects to incur about $10 million to $12 million of nonrecurring costs related to efficiency improvement throughout the year.
Fisher already incurred $1.9 million of those costs in the first quarter.

In the first quarter, Fisher's net income more than doubled to $11 million or $0.53 cents per fully diluted share, compared with net income of $4.5 million, or $0.27 per fully diluted share in last year's first quarter.
First-quarter sales increased only two percent to $526.7 million, compared with sales of $516 million in the first three months of 1996.

Fisher said sales growth in its primary market, scientific research, was partially offset by the adverse currency impact of the strong dollar and by lower sales in the soft U.S. clinical-laboratory market.
